greeting.text: Hello! I'm your academic assistant. How can I support you today?
tips: Ask about study strategies
Get time management advice
Discuss financial concerns

gratitude.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Feel free to ask anytime.

farewell.text: Take care! Remember I'm always here when you need academic support.

general.text:
I can help you with several topics. Just ask me about:

• Study tips and learning strategies
• Time management and organization
• Academic challenges
• Financial concerns and aid
• Motivation and goal setting

For example, try saying: 'I need help with studying' or 'I'm feeling overwhelmed'.

LOW.text: Your academic progress looks steady. Here are some ways to maintain your momentum:
tips: Review your notes within 24 hours of each lecture
Set aside 2-3 dedicated study hours daily
Form a small study group for challenging subjects
Use active recall instead of passive reading
resources: Peer Tutoring Program - sign up online

MEDIUM.text: I notice some academic challenges. Let's work on a plan to get you back on track:
tips: Schedule a meeting with your academic advisor this week
Visit professors during office hours for extra help
Consider reducing your course load next semester
Join a study group for your most difficult subject

HIGH.text: ⚠️ ACADEMIC ALERT: Your performance requires immediate intervention. Please take these urgent steps within the next 24-48 hours:
tips: STEP 1: Contact your academic advisor TODAY for an emergency meeting. Call the advising office at (555) 123-4567 or visit in person. Explain your situation and ask about academic recovery options.
STEP 2: Email all your professors immediately. Explain your circumstances, ask about extra credit opportunities, and request guidance on how to improve your grades before the next grading period.
STEP 3: Visit the tutoring center TODAY. Get help with your most challenging subjects. The center is open 9am-7pm in the library, first floor. No appointment needed for walk-ins.

STEP 4: Review your study habits completely. Create a new study schedule dedicating at least 3-4 hours daily to your most difficult courses. Use active learning techniques like practice problems and self-testing.
STEP 5: Attend ALL office hours this week for every course you're struggling with. Come prepared with specific questions and a list of topics you don't understand.
STEP 6: Complete and submit ALL pending assignments within 48 hours, even if late. Partial credit is better than zeros.
STEP 7: Check your academic standing and understand the consequences. If you're on probation, you need to know the requirements to continue your studies.

HIGH.text: ⚠️ FINANCIAL EMERGENCY: Your situation needs immediate attention. Please act within the next 24 hours:
tips: STEP 1: Visit the Financial Aid Office TODAY before 5pm. Go to Room 220 in the Administration Building. Bring any documents you have about your financial situation. Tell them you need emergency assistance and ask about all available options.

STEP 2: Apply for emergency financial aid immediately. The application is online at financialaid.edu/emergency or you can fill out a paper form at the Financial Aid Office. This process takes 24-48 hours, so apply NOW.

STEP 3: Speak with the Dean of Students about emergency options. The Dean's Office (Room 300) can access additional funds and resources. Explain your situation clearly and ask about the Student Crisis Fund.

STEP 4: Contact the Bursar's Office about payment deadlines. If you have an upcoming tuition deadline, ask about emergency extensions or payment plans. Don't miss deadlines - it could affect your enrollment.
STEP 5: Apply for all available scholarships immediately. Even small amounts help. Check the scholarship database and apply for anything you qualify for, even if the deadline is soon.
STEP 6: Visit the Student Employment Office about immediate job opportunities. Some on-campus jobs can start quickly. Ask about work-study and non-work-study positions.
STEP 7: Contact your family and support network. Sometimes they can provide temporary help or advice you haven't considered.
STEP 8: If you're facing housing or food insecurity, visit the Basic Needs Center (Student Union, Room 150) for immediate assistance with food, housing, and other essentials.

LOW.text: Your time management habits are working well. Here's how to keep it up:

Review and adjust your schedule weekly

MEDIUM.text: Time management could be improved. Try these practical strategies:
tips: Create a fixed daily study schedule and stick to it
Reduce non-essential commitments temporarily
Use the 2:1 ratio (2 hours study to 1 hour work)
Set specific, achievable goals for each study session

HIGH.text: ⚠️ TIME MANAGEMENT CRISIS: Your schedule is critically impacting your academics. Take these steps TODAY:
tips: STEP 1: Meet with your academic advisor IMMEDIATELY. Call the advising office at (555) 123-4567 and ask for an emergency appointment. Bring your current schedule and all course syllabi. Discuss whether you need to reduce your course load or take a leave of absence.

STEP 2: Create an EMERGENCY STUDY PLAN for this week. List all upcoming deadlines and prioritize them by due date and weight. Focus only on the most critical assignments that will have the biggest impact on your grades.
STEP 3: Contact your professors TODAY. Email them explaining your situation and ask about extensions on upcoming deadlines. Be honest about your struggles and show them your plan to catch up.
STEP 4: Use a time-blocking method for the next 7 days. Schedule every hour from 8am to 10pm. Include classes, meals, sleep, and dedicated study blocks. Follow this schedule strictly - no exceptions.
STEP 5: Eliminate ALL non-essential activities temporarily. This includes social events, extracurriculars, and entertainment. Your priority is catching up academically.
STEP 6: If you're working, consider reducing work hours temporarily. Speak with your employer about your academic situation and ask for reduced hours for the next 2-3 weeks.
STEP 7: Work with the university's time management coach. Schedule a session this week by calling the Student Success Center at (555) 789-0123. They can help you create a sustainable schedule.
STEP 8: Use the Pomodoro technique for ALL study sessions. Study for 25 minutes, break for 5 minutes. This prevents burnout and maintains focus during intense study periods.
STEP 9: Identify your most productive hours and schedule your most difficult subjects during those times. If you're a morning person, study challenging material before noon.
STEP 10: Check in with your advisor again in 3 days to report progress and adjust your plan as needed.

LOW.text: Staying motivated is important. Here are some ideas to keep your momentum:
tips: Connect with student clubs and organizations
Set small, achievable weekly goals
Find a study buddy or accountability partner
Remind yourself of your long-term career goals

MEDIUM.text: Loss of motivation is common and manageable. Here's how to address it:
tips: Speak with a counselor about motivation strategies
Take a career assessment test to explore options
Talk to professors in your major field
Join a student support group

HIGH.text: ⚠️ MOTIVATION AND WELL-BEING ALERT: Your feelings need immediate attention. Please reach out TODAY:
tips: STEP 1: Schedule a counseling appointment TODAY. Call the Counseling Center at (555) 456-7890 and ask for an emergency appointment. Tell them you're struggling with motivation and considering dropping out. They have same-day appointments for urgent situations.
STEP 2: Talk to someone you trust immediately. Call a family member, close friend, or mentor. You don't have to go through this alone. Share what you're feeling and let them support you.
STEP 3: Visit the Dean of Students office (Room 300) for immediate support. They can connect you with resources, discuss leave of absence options if needed, and help you navigate your situation.

STEP 4: DON'T make any major decisions right now. When we're struggling, we often make choices we regret later. Give yourself 48 hours before deciding about dropping out or making other major changes.
STEP 5: Take a mental health day if needed. It's okay to step back and rest. Use this time to practice self-care, sleep, and clear your mind. Then return with a fresh perspective.
STEP 6: Identify the root cause. Ask yourself: Is it the subject matter? The workload? Personal issues? Career uncertainty? Understanding WHY helps find the right solution.
STEP 7: Talk to a professor you trust. Many faculty have been through similar struggles and can offer perspective and advice. They may also provide flexibility with assignments.
STEP 8: Connect with other students. Join a support group or talk to classmates. Knowing others feel the same way can be incredibly validating and helpful.
STEP 9: Set one small goal for tomorrow. Just one. Make it achievable, like attending one class or studying for 30 minutes. Small wins build momentum.
STEP 10: Remember why you started. Think about your goals, your dreams, and what brought you to university. Sometimes reconnecting with your purpose helps rebuild motivation.

LOW.text: Here are some effective study techniques to maintain your success:
tips: Use the Pomodoro technique: 25 min focus, 5 min break
Practice active recall by testing yourself
Review material within 24 hours of learning it
Teach concepts to someone else to deepen understanding

MEDIUM.text: Here are study tips to help improve your academic performance:
tips: Create a weekly study timetable with 1-2 hours daily
Focus on your weakest topics first
Use past papers to practice and identify gaps
Remove distractions during study sessions

HIGH.text: ⚠️ EMERGENCY STUDY PLAN: You need to act quickly to get back on track. Follow this plan TODAY:
tips: STEP 1: Start with just 30 minutes of focused study TODAY. Don't overwhelm yourself. Small starts lead to momentum.
STEP 2: Identify your 3 most urgent subjects or assignments. List them in order of priority based on deadlines and impact on your grades.
STEP 3: For each priority subject, create a focused study plan. Break down what you need to learn into small, manageable chunks.
STEP 4: Use past papers and practice questions to target likely exam areas. This is the most efficient way to study when time is limited.
STEP 5: Attend ALL professor office hours this week. Come with specific questions. Professors appreciate students who seek help.
STEP 6: Find a study buddy or accountability partner. Check in with each other daily. Share what you accomplished and what you'll do next.
STEP 7: Use the Pomodoro technique for every study session. 25 minutes of intense focus, 5 minute break. This prevents burnout.
STEP 8: Create a dedicated study space free from distractions. Put your phone away, close unnecessary tabs, and focus completely.
STEP 9: Test yourself regularly, don't just re-read notes. Use flashcards, practice problems, and explain concepts out loud.
STEP 10: Get help immediately when stuck. Visit the tutoring center, ask classmates, or email professors. Don't let confusion pile up.
resources: Tutoring Center - Walk-ins welcome, Library 1st floor, open 9am-7pm

LOW.text: Taking care of your mental health is important for academic success. Here are some wellness tips:
tips: Take short breaks during study sessions
Stay connected with friends and family
Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep each night
Practice mindfulness or deep breathing

MEDIUM.text: Mental health support is available when you need it. Here are your options:
tips: Schedule a counseling appointment this week
Join a peer support group
Try stress management techniques
Talk to a trusted professor or advisor

HIGH.text: ⚠️ MENTAL HEALTH PRIORITY: Your wellbeing is the most important thing. Please reach out for support IMMEDIATELY:
tips: STEP 1: Contact counseling services RIGHT NOW. Call the Counseling Center at (555) 456-7890 and ask to speak with a crisis counselor. They have professionals available 24/7 for urgent situations.
STEP 2: If you're in crisis or need immediate help, call the 24/7 Crisis Hotline at 1-800-555-HELP. Trained counselors are available any time, day or night.
STEP 3: You don't have to struggle alone. Help is available and people care about you. Reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness.

STEP 4: Visit the Dean of Students office (Room 300) for immediate support and resources. They can help with academic accommodations, leave of absence options, and connecting you with mental health services.
STEP 5: If you're having thoughts of harming yourself, call 988 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. Your safety is the absolute priority.
STEP 6: Talk to someone you trust right now - a friend, family member, RA, or professor. Tell them what you're experiencing. Sometimes just sharing helps.
STEP 7: Practice immediate self-care. If you're overwhelmed, step away from academics for 24 hours. Sleep, eat well, go outside, do something you enjoy.
STEP 8: Contact your professors about your situation. Most will work with you on deadlines and accommodations if you communicate honestly.
STEP 9: Consider taking a mental health day or short break. It's okay to prioritize your wellbeing over academics temporarily.
STEP 10: Remember that mental health challenges are treatable and temporary. With proper support, things can and will get better.

HIGH.text: ⚠️ HIGH RISK ALERT: Your situation requires immediate attention. The critical factors are: {factors}. Please take these steps TODAY:
tips: STEP 1: Schedule an emergency meeting with your academic advisor immediately. Call (555) 123-4567 and explain your risk level. They need to know you're in a critical situation.
STEP 2: Develop an action plan TODAY. List each risk factor and specific steps to address it. Be concrete and set deadlines for each step.
STEP 3: Contact the Student Success Team. A success coach will work with you intensively. Call (555) 789-0123 to request immediate support.
STEP 4: Use ALL available support resources simultaneously. Don't wait - use tutoring, counseling, advising, and financial aid all at once.
STEP 5: Communicate with your professors. Email them today explaining your situation and asking for guidance on improving your standing.
STEP 6: Review your academic standing and understand the consequences. Know exactly what you need to do to avoid academic probation or dismissal.
STEP 7: Create a daily schedule for the next 30 days. Include classes, study time, appointments with support services, and self-care.
STEP 8: Identify one person who will check in on you daily. This could be a friend, family member, or success coach. Accountability is crucial.
STEP 9: Don't ignore any of the risk factors. Each one contributes to your overall situation. Address them all, not just the most obvious ones.
STEP 10: Remember that high risk doesn't mean failure. With intensive intervention now, you can still succeed. But you must act TODAY.

Use academic support services

HIGH.text: ⚠️ URGENT ADVICE NEEDED: Based on your HIGH risk profile, you must address these factors immediately: {factors}. Follow this urgent action plan:
tips: STEP 1: Take immediate action on ALL risk factors listed above. Each one is critical and needs attention starting TODAY.
STEP 2: Seek professional help right away. Contact academic advising, counseling, and financial aid TODAY. Don't wait or prioritize one over another.
STEP 3: Don't delay - early intervention is proven to work. Students who seek help immediately have much higher success rates.
STEP 4: Use every available resource simultaneously. This is not the time to be selective. Use tutoring, counseling, advising, and financial aid all at once.
STEP 5: Create a written action plan with specific deadlines. Share it with your advisor or success coach and update them on your progress.
STEP 6: Communicate with your professors about your situation. Be honest about your challenges and show them your action plan.
STEP 7: Check in with your advisor or success coach every 2-3 days. Regular accountability will keep you on track.
STEP 8: Don't try to solve everything alone. Let the support systems help you. That's what they're here for.
STEP 9: Be honest with yourself about what's not working. If something isn't helping, try a different approach or resource.
STEP 10: Remember that many students have been in your situation and succeeded. With intensive support now, you can too.
